climate.overview_html: Today’s diplomatic centrepiece: UN Secretary-General Guterres opened the Climate Summit 2026 on September 23 with an unprecedented demand — for the first time in UN history he called on “every government to adopt a national plan to transition away from fossil fuels” aligned with 1.5°C, with clear timelines and worker protections — a statement his outgoing term makes especially weighted as he addresses UNGA for the last time as Secretary-General. The scientific backdrop intensified overnight: a Carbon Brief analysis published September 22 shows the daily Niño 3.4 anomaly reached 3.07°C on September 19 — in a statistical tie with the all-time daily record of 3.08°C from 19 November 2015, but arriving two full months earlier in the seasonal calendar while further strengthening is still forecast through November–December. The Foster & Rahmstorf GRL warming-acceleration finding (>98% confidence, fastest acceleration of any decade in the 177-year record) continues to serve as the scientific anchor for the Nepal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA this week.

items.headline: UN Climate Summit 2026 Opens September 23: Guterres First-Ever Call for “Every Government” to Adopt National Fossil Fuel Transition Plan With Timelines & Worker Protections; Pillars: Accelerate / Finance / Protect; First Summit Framing 1.5°C Overshoot as Already Locked In
items.summary: UN Secretary-General Guterres convened the Climate Summit 2026 on September 23, 2026, bringing together heads of state and government from major economies, developing nations, and vulnerable island states. In an unprecedented step, Guterres — addressing UNGA for the final time before his term ends December 31, 2026 — called on every government to adopt a national plan to transition away from fossil fuels aligned with limiting warming to 1.5°C, with plans to include clear timelines and protection for affected workers and communities. The summit's three-pillar framework: (1) accelerate the just and orderly energy transition; (2) unlock affordable climate finance for developing countries (USD 3.1–3.5 trillion/year by 2030); and (3) protect people from climate impacts in an era of acknowledged overshoot. This is the first UN climate summit to frame 1.5°C overshoot as a condition to be managed rather than a threshold to be avoided — a significant diplomatic threshold. Leaders presented updated pre-2030 NDCs, net-zero targets, and fossil fuel phase-out commitments as inputs toward COP32.

items.headline: Carbon Brief Analysis: Super El Niño Daily Niño 3.4 Anomaly Hit 3.07°C on September 19 — Tied with All-Time Daily Record (3.08°C, 19 Nov 2015) but Two Months Earlier in Calendar; August 2026 Monthly Anomaly 2.45°C (Higher Than Peak of Every Prior El Niño Except 2015–16 & 1877–78); Further Strengthening Forecast
items.summary: Carbon Brief analysis using NOAA daily SST data finds the Niño 3.4 daily anomaly reached 3.07°C on September 19, 2026 — placing it in a statistical tie with the previous all-time daily record of 3.08°C set on 19 November 2015 during the 2015–16 El Niño event. Critically, the 2026 record arrived approximately two months earlier in the seasonal calendar than the 2015 record, while official forecasts continue to indicate further strengthening through October–December 2026. August 2026 had a monthly Niño 3.4 anomaly of approximately 2.45°C — higher than the peak of every prior El Niño on record except 2015–16 (peak 2.75°C) and the 1877–78 event (~2.7°C). Given that El Niño events typically peak in December–February, a further two to three months of intensification would very likely produce a new all-time record for both the monthly and daily anomaly.

items.headline: Super El Niño Multi-Model Forecast: 75% Probability of Strongest Event on Record Since 1950; OND 2026 Median Peak +2.67°C; 98% Probability Super El Niño Persists October–December; Spring 2027 Neutral Transition 55%
items.summary: Updated NOAA CPC and IRI multi-model ensemble forecasts give a 75% probability that the current Super El Niño will surpass the 1997–98 event to become the strongest on record since 1950. Median OND 2026 forecast is +2.67°C for the Niño 3.4 index. There is a 98% probability of the Super El Niño phase persisting through October–December 2026. A 55% probability of returning to neutral phase by April–June 2027 is consistent with historical post-Super El Niño patterns. Continued Atlantic hurricane season suppression, drought in eastern Australia, Indonesia, and SE Asia, and enhanced rainfall over the Horn of Africa and the US Gulf Coast are the near-term impact projections.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast for Most Land Areas; 2027 Still Forecast as Warmest Calendar Year on Record
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026. WMO confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Fastest of Any Decade in 177-Year Record Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA this week.

weather.overview_html: The most significant new development is the issuance of a Joint Typhoon Warning Center Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert for INVEST 91W, located approximately 127 nautical miles south of Guam near 12.5°N 141.9°E: JTWC upgraded the disturbance to high development potential on September 23, with global models in consensus on tropical depression formation within 24–48 hours under low wind shear, strong equatorward outflow, and 29–30°C sea surface temperatures. Typhoon Dujuan’s extratropical transition completed September 23: the confirmed death toll stands at nine (Chiba Prefecture 6, Kanagawa Prefecture 3), four people remain missing, approximately 500 homes were damaged across Chiba, Kanagawa, and Ibaraki, and some areas recorded more than 800 mm of rainfall in 48 hours before the system dissipated over the Northwest Pacific. In the Atlantic: Tropical Storm Fay weakened to a tropical depression and became post-tropical on September 23, ending its lifecycle without hurricane intensity — the 2026 Atlantic season has now set the record for the longest hurricane-free run in the satellite era, surpassing September 18, 1966, entirely attributable to Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear across the main development region. New haze spread to the Philippines was noted September 22–23; no material changes in Europe wildfire, Nepal flood, or Pakistan monsoon situations.

items.source: JTWC / Pacific Disaster Center / Zoom Earth
items.headline: INVEST 91W TCFA Issued September 23: ~127 nm South of Guam; JTWC Upgraded to High; Low Wind Shear (15 kts), Good Outflow, SSTs 29–30°C; Global Models Show TD Formation Within 24–48 Hours; Northwestward Track
items.summary: The Joint Typhoon Warning Center issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert for INVEST 91W on September 23, 2026, after upgrading the system from medium to high development potential. The disturbance is located approximately 127 nautical miles south of Guam, near 12.5°N 141.9°E. Scatterometry shows a tightening low-level circulation surrounded by convection in all quadrants. Environmental conditions are highly favorable: vertical wind shear at or below 15 knots, good equatorward outflow aloft, and warm sea surface temperatures of 29–30°C. Global deterministic and ensemble models are in consensus on tropical depression formation within 24 to 48 hours with a projected northwestward track. If it develops into a named storm, it would become the 26th named system of the 2026 West Pacific typhoon season.

items.source: Japan Times / The Manila Times / Jakarta Post
items.headline: Ex-Typhoon Dujuan UPDATED September 23: ET Complete; 9 Dead (Chiba 6, Kanagawa 3); 4 Missing; ~500 Homes Damaged; >800 mm in 48 h; System Dissipating Over Northwest Pacific
items.summary: Typhoon Dujuan's extratropical transition completed by September 23, 2026, with the system dissipating over the Northwest Pacific. The confirmed death toll stands at nine: six in Chiba Prefecture and three in Kanagawa Prefecture, with four people still missing across both prefectures. Approximately 500 homes were damaged across Chiba, Kanagawa, and Ibaraki. Some parts of eastern Japan recorded more than 800 mm of rainfall over 48 hours. Dujuan made landfall on the Boso Peninsula (Chiba) on September 21 with 126 km/h sustained winds — the strongest Kanto landfall since 2019. Infrastructure assessments and search operations continue.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Fay POST-TROPICAL September 23; 2026 Atlantic Season Sets Record for Longest Hurricane-Free Stretch in Satellite Era, Surpassing September 18, 1966; Super El Niño Wind Shear Attribution Confirmed
items.summary: Tropical Storm Fay weakened to a tropical depression and became post-tropical on September 23, 2026, ending its brief lifecycle without reaching hurricane intensity. With no Atlantic hurricane having formed through September 23, 2026, the season has set the record for the longest hurricane-free stretch in the satellite era, surpassing the previous record of September 18, 1966. The absence of hurricanes through the peak of the season is attributed to Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear across the main Atlantic development region — consistent with pre-season forecasts of below-normal activity. The 2026 named storm count stands at six (Alex through Fay), all at tropical storm strength or below.

items.source: Time / ASMC ASEAN / Mongabay / Ateneo de Manila ACRI
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze ONGOING: Haze Reaches Philippines (Manila “Acutely Unhealthy”); 12 Million Blanketed; 113,336 Respiratory Cases Indonesia (Sept 9); ASEAN Level 3 Alert; Worst Indonesian Fires in 11 Years
items.summary: New development September 22–23: haze from Indonesian wildfires reached Metro Manila in the Philippines, pushing air quality to 'acutely unhealthy' levels per ACRI and Breathe Metro Manila. Status as of September 17–22 otherwise unchanged: more than 12 million people across Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam blanketed in thick smog. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of September 9. More than 200,000+ hectares burned across Borneo and Sumatra. ASEAN Level 3 (highest) alert remains active. Fires expected to continue through October under Super El Niño-driven late rainy season suppression.

items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Monsoon Flood Alert ONGOING: 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured; Flash Flood Risks KPK, Punjab, GB, Balochistan; Final Monsoon Active Phase Through Late September
items.summary: No new NDMA update September 22–23. Status as of September 15: nationwide monsoon death toll 234 dead and 596 injured since late June. Flash flood risks cover Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan. Urban flooding continues in Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi. Final monsoon active phase extends through late September.

renewables.overview_html: At WindEnergy Hamburg (September 22–25), RWE’s head of offshore wind development for Belgium and the Netherlands called for Europe-wide adoption of Contracts for Difference indexation — a mechanism already used in the UK and Belgium — noting potential savings of up to €4.4 billion across Germany’s planned 9 GW offshore wind tender pipeline by 2030. India advances large-scale transmission for renewables: CTUIL (Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd) released a Transmission Service Agreement for a 2 GW Solapur renewable energy evacuation and transmission expansion project on September 23. Germany’s flagship grid build-out: 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC offshore converter platform to NSORe + Siemens Energy on September 18 — NSORe’s second 2 GW 50Hertz contract in 2026, combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 value approximately €2.5 billion. South Korea’s offshore supply chain: LS Marine Solution’s 156.9 billion won (~US$114 million) cable contract for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi project (September 18) — its largest-ever order and the first in South Korea’s 8.2 GW Sinan belt.

items.headline: RWE at WindEnergy Hamburg September 22: Calls for Europe-Wide CfD Indexation for Offshore Wind; Up to €4.4 Billion in Savings for Germany’s 9 GW Pipeline by 2030; €2 Billion Potential Savings for 4 GW Tendered in 2027
items.summary: RWE's head of offshore wind development for Belgium and the Netherlands, An Stroobandt, called at a NedZero panel at WindEnergy Hamburg on September 22 for more widespread adoption of indexation for offshore wind Contracts for Difference across Europe. The mechanism — already implemented in the UK and Belgium and under examination in Germany — links contract strike prices to inflation indices over the operating term, reducing project cost risk for developers and enabling lower bid prices at auction. For Germany's 4 GW planned for tendering in 2027, potential cost reductions are estimated at up to €2 billion over the projects' operating lifetimes; for Germany's full 9 GW tender pipeline through 2030, the figure rises to up to €4.4 billion. Stroobandt noted it is 'important for us to have a view on the long-term and to have indexation for the full-term of a CfD.' WindEnergy Hamburg runs September 22–25 with more than 1,600 exhibitors and 43,000 participants from 100 countries.

items.headline: CTUIL Releases TSA for 2 GW Solapur Renewable Energy Evacuation and Transmission Expansion Project (India) — Selected Bidder Gets 10-Day Window to Execute Agreement and Acquire 100% SPV Equity
items.summary: Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd (CTUIL), a subsidiary of Power Grid Corporation of India, released a Transmission Service Agreement on September 23, 2026, for a 2 GW renewable energy evacuation and transmission expansion project in Solapur, Maharashtra. Following issuance of the Letter of Intent, the selected bidder will have 10 days to execute the TSA and pay the acquisition price for 100% equity shareholding in the Special Purpose Vehicle. The project is part of India's large-scale grid reinforcement program to evacuate power from the Solapur solar and wind zones and integrate it into the national grid — a critical bottleneck for India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030.

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion; Topside Rostock-Warnemünde, Jacket Vlissingen
items.summary: German TSO 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the Neptun Werft–Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe) JV and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following LanWin6 in June. Siemens Energy supplies the high-voltage components; NSORe handles system design, procurement, construction, offshore installation, and commissioning. Topside fabricated at Neptun Werft (Rostock-Warnemünde); jacket at Smulders (Vlissingen). Combined NSORe value for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion.

items.headline: LS Marine Solution Wins 156.9 Billion Won (~US$114 M) Submarine Cable Contract for 390 MW Sinan Wooi Offshore Wind Farm — South Korea’s First National Growth Fund Project; Largest-Ever LS Marine Order (2.2× FY2025 Revenue); First in 8.2 GW Sinan Belt
items.summary: LS Marine Solution secured a 156.9 billion Korean won (~US$114 million) contract on September 18 to supply and install submarine power cables for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm — its largest-ever order at 2.2 times its full-year FY2025 revenue. Sinan Wooi is the first project to receive funding from South Korea's National Growth Fund specifically for offshore wind, and marks the opening project in the government-designated 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind development belt. Cable installation scheduled 2026–2028.

items.headline: Zambia Inks 25-Year PPA for 500 MW Solar Project — EnerSynk + ZESCO Copperbelt; Zambia’s Largest-Ever Renewable Contract; Replaces Drought-Hit Zambezi Hydropower for Copper Industry
items.summary: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd signed a 25-year PPA on September 16 for a 500 MW solar PV project in Zambia's Copperbelt — the country's largest-ever renewable energy contract. The project targets the copper-mining industry's power supply chain (~70% of Zambia's total power demand). The plant reduces ZESCO's dependence on hydropower repeatedly curtailed in 2026 by drought driven by the positive IOD and Super El Niño.

science.overview_html: Two new arXiv contributions from September 20–22 strengthen the ML/TC frontier. FAST-ML (arXiv:2609.25505, September 22) by Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, and Sarhadi introduces a hybrid physics–ML framework for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting: a physically-informed dual-stream neural parameterization ingests 3D ERA5 fields to diagnose ventilation-driven shear and entropy controls, and the parameters are optimised end-to-end through a differentiable FAST intensity model, ensuring storm evolution remains governed by thermodynamic constraints — directly relevant to INVEST 91W’s imminent development and next week’s potential land-falling TC. Transfer learning for Lagrangian particle dispersion model emulators (arXiv:2609.23838, September 20, Clark et al., University of Bristol): extends a South America LPDM emulator — already ~1,000× faster than physics-based simulators — to global coverage across four world regions, enabling high-resolution greenhouse-gas inversion from satellite data without prohibitive compute costs. Slightly outside the 7-day window but uniquely significant: Gao’s TAISE framework (arXiv:2609.16493) demonstrates AI weather model-powered catastrophe risk simulation at US$130 for a 50-year run on a single GPU, an order-of-magnitude cost reduction versus traditional cat models, with >2,000 cyclonic events and cross-regional correlations absent from snapshot-based approaches. Carrying forward: Moore et al. Nature Climate Change SC-CO2 labor productivity ($41/tonne CO2) and Foster & Rahmstorf GRL warming acceleration remain the empirical backbone of the Nepal UNFCCC Loss and Damage submission at UNGA.

items.headline: FAST-ML: Hybrid Physics–ML Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting (arXiv:2609.25505) — Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi; Dual-Stream ERA5 Neural Parameterization Coupled to Differentiable FAST Intensity Model; End-to-End Optimization; Physically-Constrained Rapid Intensification Forecast
items.meta: Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi · arXiv:2609.25505 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 22 September 2026
items.summary: FAST-ML bridges data-driven efficiency with physical constraints for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting, specifically targeting rapid intensification (RI) — one of the most consequential and poorly-forecast aspects of TC prediction. A physically-informed dual-stream neural parameterization ingests 3D ERA5 atmospheric fields to diagnose two key ventilation controls: environmental vertical wind shear and the mid-level entropy deficit. These parameters are then fed into a differentiable implementation of the Coupled Hurricane Intensity Prediction System (CHIPS/FAST) intensity model, with parameters optimized end-to-end through the coupled architecture. By embedding physical constraints directly into the learning objective, FAST-ML ensures storm evolution remains governed by thermodynamic principles while benefiting from the flexibility of neural network parameterization. This hybrid approach is directly relevant to the operational challenge posed by INVEST 91W's current development and any subsequent track/intensity forecast.

items.headline: From Regional to Global: Transfer Learning for Atmospheric Transport Emulators (arXiv:2609.23838) — Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby (U Bristol); LPDM Emulator Extended from South America to Four Global Regions; ~1,000× Faster Than Physics-Based Model; Enables High-Resolution Satellite GHG Inversion at Scale
items.meta: Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby · arXiv:2609.23838 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 20 September 2026 · University of Bristol
items.summary: Greenhouse gas emissions estimates from satellite observations require combining atmospheric concentration data with expensive physics-based Lagrangian Particle Dispersion Models (LPDMs). This paper evaluates whether a high-performance LPDM emulator previously developed for South America — running approximately 1,000× faster than the UK Met Office's NAME LPDM — can be spatially transferred to new regions via transfer learning. The authors evaluate spatial transferability across four world regions using both region-specific and multi-region models, establishing the conditions under which transfer learning successfully extends the emulator without full retraining. The result is a pathway toward global, high-resolution GHG inversion from modern satellite instruments (e.g. OCO-2, TROPOMI) at computational costs previously achievable only for regional domains.

items.headline: TAISE: AI-Driven Catastrophe Risk Modeling via Emergent Scenario Generation (arXiv:2609.16493) — Hang Gao; 50-Year Simulation on One GPU for US$130 with 2,000+ Cyclonic Events; Order-of-Magnitude Cost Reduction vs. Traditional CAT Models; Cross-Regional Correlations and Temporal Continuity Captured
items.summary: Traditional catastrophe (CAT) risk models rely on costly manual construction of extreme weather event sets, a methodology largely unchanged since the 1990s that lacks temporal continuity and cross-regional correlation. TAISE repurposes AI weather forecasting models (e.g. Pangu-Weather, GraphCast) to generate coherent continuous global atmospheric fields via self-iterative rollout, from which extreme events emerge rather than being manually constructed. A proof-of-concept 50-year simulation on a single GPU cost approximately US$130 and produced more than 2,000 cyclonic events — an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost versus conventional methods. The framework captures temporal continuity (multi-day event sequences) and cross-regional correlations absent in snapshot-based CAT model approaches. Directly applicable to the reinsurance/ILS sector, which has seen five consecutive years of insured nat-cat losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Heat-Related Labor Productivity Loss = US$41/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> (90% CI $1–108) — Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al.; Second-Largest SC-CO<sub>2</sub> Component After Heat Mortality; Agricultural Damage Revised Down to $29/tonne Using AR6
items.meta: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. · Nature Climate Change (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02749-z · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. quantify heat-related labor productivity loss as a standalone social cost of carbon component, finding a central estimate of US$41 per tonne CO₂ (90% CI $1–108) in 2025 dollars — the second-largest SC-CO₂ component after heat mortality. Agricultural damage was simultaneously revised down from US$95 to US$29 per tonne CO₂ using IPCC AR6 methods and updated dose-response functions. Losses are geographically concentrated in South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. The result has immediate implications for climate damage assessments used in litigation and regulatory cost-benefit analysis.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; >98% Confidence; Fastest Decade of Any in 177-Year Record Across Five Datasets After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal
items.meta: Foster & Rahmstorf · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Vol. 53, Issue 17 · doi:10.1029/2025GL118804 · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From All CMIP7 Models; Implications for SAI and Large-Eruption Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption's stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane oxidation pathway involving Cl radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS observations, the authors quantify CH₄ oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km, sufficient to explain the anomalous HCHO column of ~12 ppb at 30 km (~8× background). The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models; if triggered by large eruptions or proposed stratospheric aerosol injection, it could constitute a net cooling offset not captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding — Led by NOA VC + Upfront; DCVC, Lowercarbon, Dream Ventures Co-Invest; Pitches Cloud Seeding as Adaptation Tech for Data Center Water Demand and Drought Relief
items.body_html: Rainmaker, the El Segundo, California weather-modification startup, announced a $100 million Series B on September 21 led by NOA VC and Upfront Ventures with co-investment from DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures — bringing total funding to $150.3 million since its 2023 founding. Rainmaker deploys custom drone fleets to seed clouds with silver iodide or other nucleating agents; its atmospheric science and radar-specialist team determines optimal targets, seeding timing, material volumes, and precipitation zones; the company frames cloud seeding as climate adaptation rather than geoengineering, targeting drought relief in the American West and — notably — cooling and humidification services for water-hungry hyperscale data centers. The data-centre angle exploits the same demand that drove 34% of H1 2026 climate-tech VC to the Built Environment category per the CTVC/Currence report. The round will fund atmospheric research team expansion, drone fleet development, and commercial trials in the Southwest.
items.source_html: Fast Company / PR Newswire

items.title: CTVC / Currence H1’26 Climate Tech Report: $26.1 Billion Global VC in H1 2026 (+55% YoY); Data Centers 34% of Total; Deal Count at 5-Year Low (-25%); Series A up 55% to $4.5 Bn; Adaptation Funding +64% — Fastest-Growing Sub-Vertical
items.body_html: CTVC (now Currence) published its H1’26 Climate Tech Investment & Innovation Report on September 21, 2026, finding total global venture investment reached $26.1 billion in H1 2026 — up 55% year-on-year and the strongest first half since 2022 — driven overwhelmingly by data-centre infrastructure. The Built Environment category grew more than 800% and overtook Energy as the largest funding vertical, with Semafor framing the pattern as the “speed-to-power race”: as gas turbine lead times stretch to 5–8 years, data-center developers are driving demand for low-carbon firm power sources — advanced nuclear, superhot geothermal, long-duration storage — that can be contracted faster. Deal count fell 25% to a 5-year low; the 10 largest rounds took 42% of all H1 2026 investment. Series A rose 55% to $4.5 billion on nuclear appetite; adaptation funding grew 64% — the fastest-growing sub-vertical — consistent with the accelerating Super El Niño and record-insured-loss environment.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion — Fifth Consecutive Year of >$100 Billion Global Insured Nat-Cat Losses
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20, 2026 highlights three developments in the catastrophe bond and ILS market: MembersCap launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel industry loss warranty (ILW) structure designed to expand ILS investor access; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a previously unbondable peril, representing a structural expansion of the cat bond market’s risk frontier; and CalPERS’ insurance-linked securities holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026, cementing its position as the largest institutional investor in the cat bond asset class — all in the context of the fifth consecutive year of global insured natural catastrophe losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Project Athena Targeting 750°F (400°C) at Newberry Volcano, Oregon
items.body_html: Mazama Energy raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital (John Arnold’s fund) and Doerr Capital. ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier, SiteGround Capital, H. Barton Asset Management, and the Jeffrey and Marieke Rothschild Foundation also participated. Mazama holds the record for the hottest EGS ever built — a 629°F (331°C) well at Newberry Volcano in 2025; Project Athena targets 750°F (400°C), where a single well can deliver up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F well using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells — attributes increasingly attractive to data-center developers seeking firm low-carbon baseload.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently insured. The Alliance will develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric instruments for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 669,118 ha per EFFIS, with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics said the Alliance would not close the protection gap without mandatory natural-hazard cover.
items.source_html: Green Central Banking / The Insurer

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating external power supplies and batteries; the device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data — directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and NATO dual-use energy security.
